status: retrospective secondary analysis, fixed before inferential analysis of the downloaded values
source: D'Angelo et al. Nature Communications (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-67657-w, Experiment 3; OSF ytga5, file p5un6
source_data_unit: 30 participant rows; yes counts per participant/task/stimulation/asynchrony and published fitted widths; aggregate counts, not ordered trial-level records
primary_hypothesis: For each participant i, width(i,t,f) = c(i,t) * tau(i,f), with task multiplier c fixed across stimulation conditions
primary_population_test: Two-sided one-sample t test of mean(d)=0, 95% Student-t confidence interval; this tests a necessary population implication, not individual equality
secondary_tests: Signed-rank test and bootstrap confidence interval of mean primary contrast
Low/sham and high/sham task-by-stimulation log contrasts, with Holm correction across these two follow-ups
TOST against illustrative log-ratio margins log(1.10), log(1.20), and log(1.30); margins are sensitivity analyses, not independently calibrated experience thresholds
Participant-level observed discrepancies and paired task effect correlation; correlation is inherited from the original analysis and not the new result
Reconstruct binomial psychometric widths from aggregate counts before treating source width rows as aligned with count rows

Joint binomial Gaussian-response model comparing shared within-person frequency gain versus task-specific gain; use parametric bootstrap if source-count alignment and numerical identifiability checks permit
data_checks: Verify SHA256 hashes against OSF API metadata
Check all 30 participant IDs and count values are present, integer, between 0 and 10
Confirm published width means against primary article
Do not infer row-by-row counts-width linkage solely from agreement of means
Preserve duplicated source TBW column labels and document mapping
interpretation_limits: The strict multiplicative width bridge is an added hypothesis; the original BCI model with common sensory uncertainty does not imply this equality
Group mean equality and equivalence do not imply equality for every individual
Published fitted widths lack uncertainty estimates
Binomial count modeling assumes conditional trial independence; ordered trials/block data are unavailable
Task reports are operational endpoints, not complete measures of experience
Stimulation treatment effects do not uniquely identify alpha mediation, efference-copy consumers, or UCT versus GNW/IIT/HOT
